transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-21 09:30 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Jamie Chen (Redwood AE), Rohan Patel (Redwood SE), Aisha Rahman (Lantana - Head of ML), Ben Torres (Lantana - Platform Eng), Maya Singh (Lantana - CISO)

Summary (auto): Initial discovery for Redwood Dedicated - Lantana is evaluating reserved GPU capacity for inference of customer-facing LLM assistants and internal embedding/indexing. Main topics: isolation (VPC/on-prem), burst strategy, scaling, SLA/cost tradeoffs, security requirements (SOC2, KMS), and next steps for pricing and benchmarks.

[00:00] Jamie Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Jamie from Redwood, AE. With me is Rohan, our solutions engineer.
[00:12] Rohan Patel: Hey, morning. Quick agenda - understanding current stack, what workloads you want to move to Dedicated, isolation and compliance needs, and then talk about burst/scale and pricing.
[00:27] Aisha Rahman: Hi all, thanks. I'm Aisha - we run the ML team at Lantana. Quick context: we have a customer support assistant and an R&D search/semantic layer powered by embeddings. Currently mostly on-prem for PII-heavy stuff, some models in AWS EKS. We're exploring Redwood Dedicated because we want reserved GPUs and better latency guarantees.
[00:45] Ben Torres: Ben here - platform. We're on EKS with nodes in us-east-1, want to avoid noisy neighbors, and need predictable throughput during peak.
[00:55] Maya Singh: Maya, CISO - I'll focus on compliance questions. SOC2, data residency, audit logs, KMS.
[01:05] Jamie Chen: Great. Aisha, can you describe expected QPS/peak token rates and model footprint? Even rough numbers help.
[01:15] Aisha Rahman: Sure. For support assistant, steady-state is around 20 req/s, peaks ~120 req/s during mornings. Average prompt+response is ~500 tokens, sometimes up to 2k for long context. We use a 13B open model variant in prod. Embeddings job is batch - nightly indexing that hits about 50k docs, can be batched.
[01:38] Rohan Patel: Thanks. So two workload patterns - interactive low-latency generation and large batch embedding jobs. With Dedicated we can reserve GPU pools for the interactive model and have a separate pool for batch/embeddings, or rely on burst capacity. How sensitive is the latency? P95 targets?
[01:55] Aisha Rahman: For live chat we need P95 < 600ms for typical turns; ideally < 400ms. For embeddings, throughput and cost are more important.
[02:05] Ben Torres: Also want autoscale to protect against noisy neighbors - that was a pain with our current managed endpoints.
[02:12] Rohan Patel: Right. A lot of customers use Dedicated reserved capacity with a burst pool. You reserve a base capacity for predictable traffic and we provide configurable burst policies for overflow. Burst is backed by spare capacity in our fleet or short-term spot-like GPUs. It can be limited by duration and rate.
[02:28] Jamie Chen: Just to clarify nomenclature - we provide Dedicated (reserved capacity) and a Managed burst layer. If you need absolute isolation we also support Private deployment options (VPC or on-prem).
[02:41] Maya Singh: On isolation - our legal team requires log access and KMS, plus clear data handling. For support assistant, we keep PII; can we guarantee no model weights or customer data leaves our VPC?
[02:54] Rohan Patel: For Dedicated in a cloud-hosted model, compute lives in Redwood-managed infrastructure but we can put your Dedicated pool in a customer VPC peering model (we call it VPC peered Dedicated) so network paths are private. For stricter requirements, our Private deployment runs the control-plane in your VPC or on-prem. There are trade-offs in operational burden.
[03:12] Maya Singh: When you say VPC peered Dedicated - is that the same as bringing your own subnet? Who manages the hosts?
[03:20] Rohan Patel: We manage the hosts. You provide VPC peering and subnets, we deploy into that networking construct so traffic stays within your VPC boundary. We can integrate with your KMS for encrypted volumes and TLS termination.
[03:33] Ben Torres: That sounds promising. Any differences in SLA for peered vs fully private?
[03:40] Jamie Chen: SLA is similar for Dedicated; Private on-prem has a different support model. We'll surface those in the contract.
[03:47] Aisha Rahman: Cost - curious how we should think about for our mix of interactive plus large nightly batches. Do we need two dedicated pools?
[03:56] Rohan Patel: There are a few patterns. One is single Dedicated pool with instance types tuned for inference and autoscaling across queueing; batching helps embeddings. Another is split pools: one lower-latency optimized for generation (dedicated A100/4g-like nodes) and another for throughput embeddings (higher-density instances). We can model costs given your QPS and token distribution.
[04:16] [04:16] (background: someone typing)
[04:19] Aisha Rahman: Our engineering prefers splitting to keep SLAs tight for chat.
[04:24] Jamie Chen: Makes sense. For P95 latency targets, Rohan - we'd recommend pinning the chat model to a lower concurrency VM profile and enabling KV cache/prefix caching. That reduces repeated context compute.
[04:37] Rohan Patel: Yes. Also quantization profiles can reduce memory and increase density. We'll run a workload-aware quantization suggestion. But need to validate accuracy/regression.
[04:47] Ben Torres: About burst - how long can burst handle sustained peaks?
[04:52] Rohan Patel: Burst can sustain for short windows (minutes to tens of minutes) depending on fleet availability. For consistent daily peaks, we recommend increasing reserved commit so you're not taxed on burst pricing.
[05:03] Maya Singh: On encryption and audit logs - we need per-request audit trails, ability to redact the payloads in logs, and KMS integrations. Also retention policies on logs - 7 years is typical for us.
[05:17] Jamie Chen: We provide request-level logs, but retention and redaction policies are configurable. For PII removal we can integrate with an ingestion scrubber or enable selective logging. KMS is supported for key management; we also support customer-managed HSM options in Private deployments.
[05:33] Aisha Rahman: Performance testing - we'd want a benchmark: 1) chat latency with our prompts, 2) nightly embedding throughput. Can you run benchmarks in your Dedicated environment or do we need to provide payloads?
[05:46] Rohan Patel: We typically ask customers to provide representative payloads and we run benchmarks in a sandbox Dedicated pool. For security reasons we can run with masked data or in your VPC peered environment. We'll need sample payload distributions, max context lengths, and concurrency patterns.
[06:01] Ben Torres: How about rollout strategy? We want canary deploys and automatic fallback to smaller models if latency spikes.
[06:09] Rohan Patel: Redwood supports route-level rollouts, canary percentage, and automatic fallback policies to compatible model variants. We also expose tracing and token-level latency so you can set automated policies.
[06:21] Aisha Rahman: What about model updates - we need to pin model versions for compliance and be able to rollback quickly.
[06:28] Jamie Chen: You can pin versions per route and do progressive rollouts. We keep model artifacts immutable per version. Rollbacks are supported via console or API and can be automated.
[06:37] Maya Singh: SLA penalties - are they financial? We need to see the SLA language.
[06:42] Jamie Chen: Yes, for Dedicated we provide SLA terms with service credits. We'll share the standard SLA in the security pack.
[06:49] [06:49] (brief pause)
[06:52] Rohan Patel: Quick question on embedding consistency: are you expecting the nightly batch to be real-time streamed or a bulk job?
[06:58] Aisha Rahman: Bulk job nightly but occasionally have ad-hoc reindexes during migrations.
[07:04] Rohan Patel: Ok - for bulk we can optimize with larger batch sizes and multi-GPU sharding. For ad-hoc reindexes, a burst path or temporarily scaling the embeddings pool is typical.
[07:14] Ben Torres: For procurement timing - we are budgeting for Q4 procurement window and want service start early Q1 2027. Is that timeline OK?
[07:23] Jamie Chen: Yes, that's reasonable. Contracting + onboarding typically 4-8 weeks depending on compliance review. Private/on-prem adds extra time.
[07:31] Maya Singh: A few security specifics: 1) We require SSO via SAML/SCIM for RBAC. 2) Audit logs must be exportable to our SIEM. 3) We need proof of SOC2 Type II and pen test results.
[07:47] Rohan Patel: We support SAML/SCIM, log export to Splunk/Datadog/your SIEM. We'll include SOC2 Type II report and recent pen test summary in the security pack.
[07:57] Aisha Rahman: One more technical - KV cache semantics. Our prompt patterns reuse long user context often; how is KV cache handled across pods and after failovers?
[08:07] Rohan Patel: Our runtime manages KV cache per request session. For Dedicated pools we use shared in-memory cache within an instance and we persist a checkpoint to a distributed cache for cross-node warm starts. That said, in some failure modes you'll see cold starts; we recommend sticky routing for sessions that need very low latency.
[08:25] Ben Torres: Sticky routing might complicate scaling. Does it reduce ability to autoscale horizontally?
[08:30] Rohan Patel: There's a tradeoff - sticky routing improves latency but concentrates load. For most use cases we combine prefix caching and smart routing to balance stickiness with load.
[08:40] Maya Singh: Compliance again - can we have a dedicated tenant with separate metadata and logs?
[08:45] Jamie Chen: Yes, Dedicated gives tenant isolation and we can partition logs by customer. Private on-prem gives you full control.
[08:51] Aisha Rahman: What about failover across regions? We have customers in EU and NA and need geo failover.
[08:58] Rohan Patel: We support multi-region Dedicated deployments and smart routing by region. For strict data residency you can pin certain routes to a region.
[09:08] Ben Torres: Pricing - any ballpark per-GPU or per-reserved-unit?
[09:13] Jamie Chen: We'll share a detailed pricing PDF. Ballpark, reserved pool costs are a commit (monthly/annual) tied to instance types. Burst is usage-based. We'll model against your numbers and give a cost per effective token.
[09:25] Aisha Rahman: For the benchmark we'd want to validate P95 under load. Can we run a two-week pilot?
[09:31] Jamie Chen: We do pilots - often 2-6 weeks depending on scope. For this, a 2-week sandbox Dedicated with limited commit to validate latency and throughput is a good fit.
[09:41] Maya Singh: Data handling in pilot - we'd need to mask PII or run in our VPC peered sandbox.
[09:47] Rohan Patel: Both supported. For masked data we can run quickly; for VPC peered runs we'll coordinate network setup.
[09:56] Aisha Rahman: Ok. Any notable limitations we should be aware of?
[10:00] Rohan Patel: A couple: 1) Burst availability isn't infinite during large industry-wide events. 2) Very large context lengths (8k+) may require special instance types and tuning. 3) Quantization can impact accuracy - we'll validate.
[10:14] Ben Torres: Good to know. For procurement we'll need a security questionnaire filled out.
[10:18] Jamie Chen: We'll send the security pack and the Azure/AWS network diagram templates.
[10:22] Aisha Rahman: Great. Anything else from the Redwood side?
[10:26] Rohan Patel: I'll prepare a proposed benchmark plan and list of data samples we need. Also we'll recommend an initial Dedicated sizing (nodes, GPUs) for your traffic pattern.
[10:36] Maya Singh: From Lantana, we'll gather the infra diagram, sample payloads (masked), and a list of stakeholders for the procurement thread.
[10:43] Jamie Chen: Awesome. Let's recap next steps.
[10:46] Jamie Chen: Action items - I'll send pricing and security docs; Rohan will prepare the benchmark plan; Maya/Aisha will share infra diagram and sample payloads. Schedule a technical deep dive for the infra team on 2026-11-02 if that works?
[10:58] Aisha Rahman: Works for us.
[11:01] Ben Torres: Yep.
[11:02] Maya Singh: Sounds good.
[11:05] Jamie Chen: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up by EOD with docs and a calendar invite for the deep dive.

Recap / Notes:
- Primary ask: Dedicated reserved GPUs for low-latency chat (P95 <600ms target) and separate pool or burst strategy for embeddings batch jobs.
- Networking: Prefer VPC peered Dedicated; if more strict, consider Private on-prem deployment.
- Security: SAML/SCIM, KMS integration, audit logs export, SOC2 Type II, pen test summary.
- Benchmarks: Redwood to run sandbox benchmarks with masked payloads or in VPC peered environment.
- Timeline: Budget Q4, onboarding early Q1 2027, pilot 2 weeks recommended.
